label: <DEL> step of sequences starting with g (sparse, needs extra cues)
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (98% of mass) and only when the first original token is g (99.7% of mass). Its output at that step is first_tok, so it acts as a recall-g-first signal. It is very sparse: only about 1% of g-initial delimiter steps activate, so the predicate gets recall 0.97 but precision 0.01. Activation is more likely and larger when z is also early (orig(1) or orig(2)), when L is 6-8, when there are few digits, and when the last tokens are v/w/y/d/x. The top example is g z r w y v (act 2.16). No combination of these cues I tried got precision above about 0.22 (best F1 about 0.26 for g, then z at position 1 or 2, plus w or v present). Magnitude goes up with z at position 1 and v/w late in the sequence. Never fires in the copy phase, and fires on just 3 original-phase steps, all tiny. Does not fire for other first tokens.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=g (+3.50), orig0=g (+2.67), orig2=z (+2.37), prev_tok=v (+2.16), orig1=z (+2.12), orig3=y (+1.62). Lower it: in_count=1 (-2.07), in_first=0 (-1.90), orig5=- (-1.24), n_digits=2 (-1.17).
